question: What is the common anatomical term for the rectouterine pouch?
explanation: The rectouterine pouch is commonly referred to as the pouch of Douglas or the cul-de-sac. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h1)

question: Why does fluid in the pelvic cavity tend to accumulate in the cul-de-sac?

options.A: It is the highest point of the abdominal cavity.
options.B: It is actively secreted by the rectum.
options.C: It is the lowest point of the female peritoneal cavity.
options.D: It is pumped there by muscular contractions of the fallopian tubes.

explanation: Due to its dependent anatomical position, the cul-de-sac is the lowest point of the peritoneal cavity, causing fluid to pool there by gravity. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common cause of blood accumulation in the cul-de-sac?
explanation: Blood frequently accumulates in the cul-de-sac due to a leaking or ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h2)

question: How does pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) typically contribute to cul-de-sac fluid abnormalities?

options.A: By causing retrograde flow of purulent exudate through the fallopian tubes
options.B: By halting all fluid production in the peritoneal cavity
options.D: By causing complete atrophy of the ovaries

explanation: In PID, purulent exudate can travel out through the fimbriae of the infected fallopian tubes and pool in the pouch of Douglas. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h2)

question: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections is strongly linked to tubal damage and subsequent pelvic inflammatory disease?
explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is a primary STI known to cause ascending infections leading to tubal damage and pelvic inflammatory disease. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h3)

question: How does endometriosis contribute to abnormalities in the pouch of Douglas?

options.A: By causing endometrial implants, chocolate cysts, and pelvic adhesions
options.B: By causing complete closure of the urethra
options.C: By increasing the systemic blood pressure

explanation: Endometriosis leads to functional endometrial tissue outside the uterus, resulting in implants, cysts, and adhesions in the pelvis including the cul-de-sac. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h3)

question: Why might a patient with significant hemoperitoneum from a ruptured ectopic pregnancy experience shoulder pain?

options.A: Referred pain caused by diaphragmatic irritation from blood in the peritoneal cavity
options.B: Direct injury to the shoulder joint during pelvic examination
options.C: Muscle strain from lifting heavy objects

explanation: Blood in the peritoneal cavity irritates the diaphragm, causing referred pain that is frequently felt in the shoulder. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h4)

question: What causes the symptom of rectal pressure and tenesmus in patients with cul-de-sac fluid collections or abscesses?

options.A: Mass effect and pressure of the fluid against the adjacent rectum
options.B: Direct infection of the anal sphincter

explanation: Fluid or abscess accumulation in the pouch of Douglas exerts direct physical pressure on the posterior rectum, causing rectal pressure and tenesmus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h4)

question: What is indicated by extreme tenderness upon moving the cervix during a bimanual pelvic examination?

options.A: Cervical motion tenderness, suggesting PID or ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Cervical motion tenderness (chandelier sign) indicates pelvic inflammation or irritation often seen in PID or ectopic pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h5)

question: Which diagnostic imaging tool is most effective for visualizing free fluid and masses in the cul-de-sac?
explanation: Transvaginal ultrasonography provides high-resolution imaging of pelvic organs, free fluid in the pouch of Douglas, and adnexal structures. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h5)

question: When is medical management with methotrexate typically considered appropriate for an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: When the patient is hemodynamically stable with an unruptured ectopic pregnancy
options.B: When the patient is in active hemorrhagic shock with a ruptured tube
options.C: When the pregnancy is in the third trimester
options.D: When the patient has severe active liver disease

explanation: Methotrexate is used medically for stable patients with unruptured ectopic pregnancies to dissolve the pregnancy tissue safely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h6)

question: What is a primary surgical goal when treating a large, infected abscess localized in the pouch of Douglas?

options.A: Drainage of the purulent collection and infection control

explanation: Surgical management of a pelvic abscess focuses on draining the infected collection and controlling the source of sepsis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h6)

question: What is the primary physiological threat associated with a ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Hypovolemic shock from massive internal hemorrhage

explanation: Rupture of a tubal ectopic pregnancy can cause rapid internal bleeding, leading to life-threatening hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h7)

question: Which immediate nursing intervention is crucial when a patient shows signs of shock due to internal bleeding?

options.A: Establishing large-bore IV access and initiating rapid fluid resuscitation
options.B: Instructing the patient to walk around the ward
options.D: Discharging the patient with pain relievers

explanation: Large-bore IV access and rapid fluid resuscitation are vital emergency steps to restore circulating blood volume and stabilize blood pressure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h7)

question: What key preventative educational topic should nurses emphasize to reduce the incidence of pelvic inflammatory disease and tubal scarring?

options.A: Safe sexual practices and early treatment of sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Avoiding all physical exercise for life

explanation: Educating patients on safe sex and prompt STI treatment prevents ascending infections that cause tubal scarring and PID. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h8)

question: Which of the following is an important element of holistic nursing care for a patient experiencing reproductive loss due to an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Providing compassionate psychological support and counseling referrals
options.B: Ignoring emotional responses to focus solely on wound care
options.D: Minimizing the significance of the diagnosis

explanation: Compassionate emotional support and counseling are essential to help patients cope with the grief and psychological impact of reproductive loss. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h8)
